title: Advice: listening, books and being melodic
summary: Read the jazz authors and become more melodic.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: What advice would you offer these young guys now that are into playing, besides listening?

Well, I think the number one thing is listening. But be very careful what you're listening to. And it's not too hard to know what to listen. There's certainly plenty of books that tell you who the good people in jazz are. I mean, Ira Gitler and --Leonard Feather.

Dan Morgenstern, that's the man I was trying to think of, have written very good books, give very good discographies. Dave Baker's Jazz Book has got good discography in it. Well, most of those jazz books have good discographies and guys listen to those records very carefully, and above all, I think that music has gotten so technical, gotten so fast, so high powered, that it's gone off in this offshoot direction of what they call synthesized music, fusion music, that the only direction for the mainstream of jazz to go is to get more melodic and more lyrical. They're not going to get faster, they're not going to get louder, they're not going to get farther out harmonically. The only thing they're not doing as much as they could is getting more musical.

So I think if somebody wants to take a gamble on the future he should gamble on being more musical. And by that I mean, learning to play lyrically, whether you want to play a melody or -- whatever you play should have a melodic line and
a feeling for that. And the way to develop that is to listen to people who did it well. And that has not happened too much in the last 20 years. So you do have to go back pretty far to hear that.
